messages.subject: Cross-validation in lavaan?
parts:
I'm trying to do some cross-validation with lavaan. What I want to do is fit a model:

training_model = sem(model, data=training_data)

Then use the parameter estimates from the training model to evaluate the fit with new data. I'm imagining it might look something like this:

validation_model = cross_val(training_model, newdata=validation_data)

The resulting model (validation_model) would ideally be of the same class as training_model.

I know I can fix the parameters in the model (e.g., y =~ 1.5*y_1), but if I fix all the parameters, I don't get any fit indices. I know some indices might not make sense if I fix all the parameters, but not all of them.

Is there a way to do this in lavaan?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Cross-validation in lavaan?
parts: I know I can fix the parameters in the model (e.g., y =~ 1.5*y_1), but if I fix all the parameters, I don't get any fit indices

The problem is that you aren't fitting the model to data.  When all the parameters are already fixed, the data have no say in the matter.  So you have to ask lavaan to lie to you, using the optim.force.converged= argument (see description in the ?lavOptions help page)

PT <- parTable(training_model) # model specification as a data.frame PT$free <- 0L # fix all parameters
PT$start <- PT$ustart <- PT$est # use estimates as starting values
PT$est <- PT$se <- NULL # remove point and standard-error estimates
## re"fit" the model
validation_model <- update(training_model, model = PT,
data = validation_data,
optim.force.converged = TRUE)
summary(validation_model)
